   ["adding-knowledge"]- Assume there are 365 days in a year, and each day is equally likely for a birthday.["end-section"]
   ["deduction"]- The first person can have any of the 365 days as their birthday.["end-section"]

   ["deduction"]- The probability that all 30 people have unique birthdays is: ["end-section"]
     \[
     P(\text{unique}) = \frac{365}{365} \times \frac{364}{365} \times \frac{363}{365} \times \dots \times \frac{336}{365}
     \]
   ["adding-knowledge"]- This can be expressed as: ["end-section"]
     \[

     \]

   \[
   6 \times 6 \times 6 = 6^3 = 216
   \] ["end-section"]

   \] ["end-section"]
